name: Meesho Ltd

ar26.what: Annual report FY26 with AGM notice (AGM 18-Sep-2026)

segments.marketplace: Zero-commission marketplace connecting ~1 million small sellers with 274 million annual buyers. Revenue: logistics/fulfilment fees charged to sellers (orders shipped through Valmo, Meesho's own logistics platform that aggregates small transport firms, and third-party couriers), seller advertising, and platform fees; plus Meesho Mall (branded products, ~1,200 brands) and Content Commerce (creators). 99.9% of revenue.
segments.newInitiatives: Low-cost local logistics network for daily essentials, digital financial services (NBFC partners lend to sellers and consumers; Meesho gives a first-loss default guarantee), AI services; Kirana Club (B2B marketplace for small retailers, acquisition announced Jul-2026, closing in Q2FY27). Loss capped at ~₹200 cr a year.

guidanceAndCall.what: NMV growth: long-term guidance of ~25% CAGR over the next five years, higher in the early years and lower later.

Flagship sale (Mega Blockbuster Sale) moves from Q2 to Q3 this year (Diwali in November): Q2FY27 NMV growth will look soft and Q3 strong; similar to trend on Q2+Q3 combined. Growth spends step up 'meaningfully' from Q2.
New initiatives: annual EBITDA-loss budget cap of ~₹200 cr; still 'pre product-market fit' in local logistics.
No short-term EBITDA guidance; LTM free cash flow is the guiding metric and should improve quarter by quarter.

Contribution margin: logistics margin being restored after the FY26 Valmo disruption; beyond that, logistics efficiencies are passed on to sellers and buyers; ads lift contribution margin. Baseline AOV decline ~5% a year as efficiencies are passed on (Q1FY27: −2%).
Fuel-price and minimum-wage increases in Q1FY27 were passed through; cost per delivered order still fell ~₹1 QoQ.

Valmo Transportation Pvt Ltd (VTPL) operates as a Goods Transport Agency (GTA) for GST; a proxy adviser questioned the GST treatment. Management: legal and accounting opinions taken, no question from any tax authority or SEBI.

history: Founded in Bengaluru by Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar as a reseller (social-commerce) app; Indian operating company Fashnear Technologies, owned by US parent Meesho Inc.
Peak losses (₹3,248 cr) as it chased users with discounts; SoftBank Vision Fund II and Fidelity among investors.
Switch to zero commission for sellers and Valmo logistics; loss cut from ₹1,675 cr to ₹328 cr; free cash flow positive in FY24.

Re-domiciled from the US to India (reverse flip): Meesho Inc. merged into the Indian company (NCLT order 27-May-2025). One-time costs: ₹1,346 cr exceptional items (ESOP modification, perquisite tax paid for founders) and ₹2,487 cr tax, giving a ₹3,942 cr loss.

IPO at ₹111 (3-5 Dec 2025; listed 10-Dec-2025): 38.29 cr new shares, ₹4,250 cr. Valmo scale-up after third-party courier consolidation cut contribution margin to 2.3% in Q3; recovered to 4.0% in Q4. ₹2,780 cr of tax paid in cash (reverse flip).
Lock-in on pre-IPO holders expired 9-Jun-2026; Kirana Club acquisition announced (Jul-2026); GTA model in Valmo Transportation.

sharesOutstanding.src: FY26 annual report notes 16 and 32; Jun-26 implied by 42.13 cr domestic-institution shares = 9.14% (Inc42, 16-Jul-2026; Screener)

accounting: Adjusted EBITDA (segment result) excludes ESOP cost (₹182 cr FY26), exceptional items (₹141 cr FY26: business-combination costs ₹102 cr and a ₹39 cr vendor settlement) and other income.

FY25 loss includes one-offs: ₹482 cr ESOP-modification charge, ₹62 cr accelerated vesting, ₹734 cr perquisite tax paid on behalf of the founders, ₹68 cr combination costs (exceptional, ₹1,346 cr) and ₹2,487 cr tax on the re-domicile.
FY26 operating cash flow (−₹3,875 cr) includes ₹2,780 cr of income tax paid on the re-domicile; company free cash flow excludes it.
Negative working capital: sellers are paid after delivery, so the platform holds the float (other liabilities ₹3,458 cr at Mar-26).
No deferred tax asset is booked on carried-forward losses (FY26 tax note).
